fail_then_pass_guidance_for_this_case: Part A (plugin_handler_test.exs AC7): the pre-fix code here is NOT 'module does not exist' (the describe block and its two tests existed before ISS-0377's fix, just with Unix-only hardcoded assertions) -- this is a fix to EXISTING behavior, so the workflow doc's plain fail-then-pass rule applies directly, NOT the 'non-existence' mutation-only carve-out. Concretely: check out the pre-fix commit (parent of 8eef01b, i.e. 64eef56 or earlier -- confirm the exact pre-fix SHA yourself), run the OLD AC7 describe block's two tests in a simulated non-Unix artifact shape (e.g. temporarily rename/relocate priv/native/wasmex.so or fake a priv_dir layout with only a .dll-named file present, or stub :code.priv_dir(:wasmex) if that's cleaner) and confirm the OLD assertions (hardcoded 'native/wasmex/src/' substring match + hardcoded 'native/wasmex.so' path) fail in that simulated shape. Then confirm the NEW (post-fix, commit 8eef01b) assertions pass against that same simulated non-Unix shape (since they derive the extension from :os.type/0 rather than hardcoding it, they should be satisfiable even when simulating a Windows-shaped artifact tree on this Linux sandbox, e.g. temporarily monkey-patching or parameterizing the extension the test looks for). If a live simulated-non-Unix run is impractical in this sandbox, the alternative explicitly given in this same handoff's routing instruction is: mutate the FIX back to the OLD broken assertion (revert just that one line/expression) and confirm that reverted version fails where the current fixed version passes -- this is the 'mutation of the fix itself' variant of the fail-then-pass proof, and is equally acceptable evidence here.

Part B (scripts/test_parallel.sh): per the design doc's own Part C note, this has no unit-testable Elixir surface -- it's bash control flow. Confirm this project's existing precedent for testing scripts/*.sh (grep test/ and scripts/ for any existing shellcheck/bats/script-level test harness) before assuming ExUnit is the only vehicle, per Part C's explicit instruction. A viable regression check: capture MIX_BUILD_PATH as logged/observed from two different partitions' environments during a real scripts/test_parallel.sh run and assert they differ (per Part C's own suggested check) -- and/or a fail-then-pass demonstration by mutating Step 1.6 out (or reverting to the pre-fix script) and showing the isolation check now fails.

Mutation is a TEMPORARY PROBE per WF-03's Step 2-4 section -- if you mutate committed files (test file assertions or the script) to demonstrate the pre-fix failure, you MUST revert the mutation and verify the revert before finishing this step. Do not leave a mutant in the tree.
